newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open sharply lower after Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open sharply lower after Wall Street.

text.p: French shares opened sharply lower on profit-taking on Friday after an overnight 1.38 percent fall on Wall Street.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 25.87 points or 1.05 percent at 2,435.38 at 0905 GMT after opening 1.2 percent lower. The CAC-40 futures contract was down 20 points at 2,444.
"I do not see any reason for people to panic. We have had quite a run. It all went up very quickly, and it is now time to pause and take profits," a broker said.
On Thursday, French shares closed at a fresh record with a 0.77 percent rise to 2,461.25 points. They have been rising sharply since December 17, when the CAC index stood at 2,193.70.
The market was also pressured by lower French bond futures.

Shares in financial group Paribas were 2.38 percent lower at 369 francs after insurer AXA said it had sold part of its Paribas stake, or 2.42 percent of the capital, for 1.1 billion francs. Axa shares were 0.67 percent lower at 356.80 francs.
